parsed.explanation: Visitor-facing exposures dominate. Entry screening: officers must refuse cases where documents cast doubt on sex, with possible permanent fraud-based ineligibility; X-markers no longer processed, passports confiscated/blocked, stranded travellers, and multiple allied governments issued trans-travel advisories — a documented, trans-specific border exposure. Facilities: the state's 2023 law lets many state-run facilities exclude trans people, and the state has no gender-identity public-accommodations or hate-crime statute, so an excluded or harassed visitor has no local remedy. Detention carries documented harm (conversion-style practices nationally, abuse in immigration custody). Offsetting: no criminalisation of trans identity or presentation; the national hate-crime statute and 2020 employment ruling still exist (though under attack); courts have enjoined several orders; no documented violence pattern against trans visitors here; birth-certificate rules are resident-facing and excluded. Universal facility exclusion plus hostile border screening without working remedy place this below the reduced-risk band.
